To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inability to replicate a satellite RNA in the host plant can be mapped to a single amino-acid change in the helper virus.
the 1a proteins of the helper viruses Fny- and Fny-CMV can support the replication and movement of the satellite WL1 in zucchini squash protoplasts and plants.
support of satellite RNA maps to the helicacease domain and is determined by a single amino acid in the helper virus RNA 1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between a virus and its molecular parasites.
the identification of the viral factors that are responsible for the replication and movement of satellite RNA.
the molecular basis of satellite RNA replication in a plant virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acid at position 978 is critical for the ability of CMV to support WL1 replication and that this amino acid is proximal to the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase domain VI of the helper virus.
the 978 amino acid of the Fny-CMV 1a protein is required for the support of WL1 RNA in zucchini plants.
the inability to provide a replication function for the WL1 satellite is due to a single amino change in the 1A protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ability of CMV to support a particular satellite RNA is determined by a single amino acid in the 1A protein of the helper virus.
the 1a proteins of Fny- CMV and Sny-CMVs are functionally equivalent, except that the Sny- CMV 1a protein is not able to recognize and support replication of WL1 satellite RNA.
the ability of CMV to support the replication and accumulation of a satellite RNA is determined by a single amino acid in the 1b protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability of a helper virus to support a satellite RNA is not a function of the host plant but of the helper virus itself.
the 1a proteins of CMV and other viruses with a tripartite genome can have a profound effect on the replication of the satellite RNAs.
the 1a helicase is a key determinant for satellite replication and that the amino acid at position 978 is a key residue that determines whether the 1a is able to support satellite replication.
